sections.h2: Which Warren County offices deal with my property tax?
sections.html:
Warren County has three offices that matter to a homeowner, all in or near Bowling Green. The PVA values the property, the sheriff sends and collects the bill, and the county clerk takes over bills still unpaid on April 15.

  • Property Valuation Administrator: 429 E. 10th Avenue, Bowling Green, KY 42101. The county's department directory lists (270) 843-3268, weekdays 8:00 to 4:30.
  • Sheriff's Office, the collector of state, county, school and district taxes: (270) 842-1633, with a tax inquiry page on its website. The business office keeps hours of 8:00 to 4:30.
  • County Clerk: P.O. Box 478, Bowling Green, KY 42102, phone (270) 842-9416, weekdays 8:00 to 4:30. It also records deeds and holds the delinquent tax list.

The clerk's own page points property tax and valuation questions to the PVA, so use that office to confirm the assessment and the clerk or sheriff to confirm what is owed.

sections.h2: What are the Warren County due dates for the 2026 tax year?
sections.html:
The sheriff published the 2026 schedule on its website. The sheriff told owners to expect bills in the first week of October, and the dates follow the statewide calendar under KRS 134.015.

  • 2 percent discount: October 1 through November 1, 2026. That window closed November 1, 2026.
  • Face amount, no discount and no penalty: November 2 through December 31, 2026.
  • 5 percent penalty: January 1 through January 31, 2027.
  • 21 percent penalty: February 1 through April 15, 2027, which combines the 10 percent penalty and the sheriff's add on fee.

The sheriff does not accept American Express. A credit or debit card costs $1.50 on payments of $60.00 or less and 2.49 percent on anything higher, and an ACH or e-check payment costs $1.50. The site updates payment data after 7:00 pm each business day, so a Friday payment may not show until Monday evening.

An owner who is selling should pay by check or ACH if possible to avoid the card percentage on a large bill.

sections.h2: What property tax rates apply in Warren County?
sections.html:
The county clerk posts a rate sheet each year. For calendar 2025 it lists real estate rates in cents per $100 of assessed value, and the county pieces are the same for every parcel.

Warren County 2025 real estate tax rates in cents per $100, from the County Clerk's rate sheet
LevyRate
State10.60
County general14.00
Library3.70
Public health2.90
Extension0.60
Conservation0.25
County levies combined21.45
School, county district52.20
School, city district84.80
City20.30

Adding the lines gives three common totals. A house outside any city pays 84.25 cents per $100. A city parcel in the county school district pays 104.55, and a city parcel in a city school district pays 137.15. Ask the PVA or the sheriff which set applies to your address.

sections.h2: How much tax does a median Warren County house pay?
sections.html:
Census QuickFacts puts the median owner occupied home at $258,000. At 84.25 cents per $100 that assessment would owe about $2,173.65 outside a city. In a city with its own school district the same assessment would owe about $3,538.47, and in a city served by the county schools about $2,697.39.

These are illustrations at the median, not predictions for any one house, since assessments can sit above or below sale prices. A homestead exemption of $49,100 lowers the taxable amount to $208,900 and saves about $413.67 a year at the 84.25 rate.

sections.h2: Who can claim the Kentucky homestead exemption in Warren County?
sections.html:
An owner who is 65 or older, or who is classified as totally disabled, can file with the Warren County PVA. The exemption is $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years and comes off the assessed value before the rates apply.

Proof of age can be a birth certificate, driver's license or passport. Disability claims need to be renewed yearly unless the owner is a veteran with a service connected disability or has been found permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems. Census QuickFacts counts 14.2 percent of Warren County residents as 65 or older.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Warren County assessment?
sections.html:
Request a conference with the PVA before anything else. The county's directory lists (270) 843-3268 for that office, and a conference with the PVA or a deputy is required under state rules before an appeal can be filed.

The tax roll is open for 13 days starting the first Monday in May. File with the County Clerk by the close of business on the day after the inspection ends. The local board of assessment appeals then hears cases between 25 and 35 days after inspection closes, and meets up to five days unless the state grants more.

  • Bring evidence about the building, such as photographs, insurance policies, construction costs and sales listings.
  • If you are paying someone to speak for you, the person must be an attorney, accountant, appraiser, licensed broker or another recognized professional, and must show written authority.
  • Ask for a written explanation of any change the board makes.

sections.h2: What happens after April 15 if a Warren County bill is unpaid?
sections.html:
The sheriff turns the bill over to the County Clerk at the close of business on April 15, and it becomes a certificate of delinquency with a lien on the property. The clerk keeps accepting payments until the annual sale. The 2026 sale was set for August 26, 2026 at 9:00 am at 429 E 10th Ave, Suite 100, with registration for buyers closing August 17, and that date has passed.

Interest accrues at 1 percent a month once the clerk has the bill. The clerk takes 10 percent of tax, penalty and interest, and the county attorney takes 20 percent once the first notice is mailed. That attorney fee is waived if the bill is paid within five business days of the transfer. A $10 fee covers recording and releasing the lien, and a third party buyer at the sale can add its own interest.

The lien stays on the land for up to 11 years whoever owns it, so a seller should clear the balance at closing and get the clerk's release. The clerk publishes a current delinquent list as a PDF.

sections.h2: What should a Warren County seller know about the county itself?
sections.html:
Warren is the fifth most populous county in Kentucky, with Bowling Green as seat and largest city. It was set up in 1796 and covers about 542 square miles of land across the Pennyroyal Plateau, with the Barren River running through Bowling Green. Interstate 65 and the Natcher Parkway, now I-165, brought an industrial boom in the 1960s and 1970s. About 72.7 percent of residents lived in urban areas in 2020.

Growth shows in the numbers. The population estimate for July 2025 is 149,375, up 11.0 percent from the 2020 base, and the county issued 1,453 building permits in 2025. Median gross rent is $1,002, and only 55.6 percent of homes are owner occupied. Median household income is $65,794 and 32.3 percent of adults have a bachelor's degree.

Work done without a permit can slow a sale. The county's Division for Building Services at 1141 State Street, (270) 843-5360, covers permits outside Bowling Green and Oakland, charging $0.15 per square foot with a $45 minimum, and it states a fine of at least $500 for starting construction without one. Bowling Green has its own building inspector.

faqs.q: Who do I pay for Warren County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Warren County Sheriff's Office, which collects state, county, school and district taxes. The business office phone is (270) 842-1633 and the hours are 8:00 to 4:30 on business days.

faqs.q: Is the 2 percent Warren County discount still open?
faqs.a: No. For the 2026 tax year it ran from October 1 through November 1, 2026, and the face amount is due through December 31. A 5 percent penalty starts January 1.

faqs.q: What does the Warren County Sheriff charge for card payments?
faqs.a: It charges $1.50 on payments of $60.00 or less and 2.49 percent on larger ones. ACH or e-check costs $1.50 per transaction, and American Express is not accepted.

faqs.q: Where does the Warren County delinquent tax sale take place?
faqs.a: At the County Clerk's office, 429 E 10th Ave, Suite 100, in Bowling Green. The 2026 sale was scheduled for August 26, 2026, and buyers had to register in advance.

faqs.q: Does Warren County have a single tax rate?
faqs.a: No. The 2025 total depends on where the house sits: 84.25 cents per $100 outside a city, 104.55 in a city with county schools, and 137.15 in a city school district. The county levies are the same in every case.
